newsitem.title: USA: Soros seeks ouster of WMX Technologies CEO.
newsitem.headline: Soros seeks ouster of WMX Technologies CEO.

text.p: Saying it is growing frustrated with the management of WMX Technologies Inc, a group led by international financier George Soros called Tuesday for the ouster of the company's chief executive and the election of four of its candidates to its board.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Soros group, which holds about 5.2 percent of the Oak Brook, Ill., garbage hauling company, said it proposed removing WMX President and Chief Executive Officer Phillip Rooney.

Describing a series of alleged contradictions by WMX executives and dissatisfaction with a recent company restructuring plan, the group said it proposed Rooney's ouster in a telephone conversation between Soros aide Stanley Druckenmiller and WMX Chairman Dean Buntrock on Saturday.
The Soros group, which has been pressing WMX for months to improve its performance, stressed that it was not seeking a hostile takeover of the company.
But it said it nominated four candidates to the WMX board in a written notice dated Monday.

The group's nominees are Harvey Karp, 69, former chief executive of Mueller Industries Inc., Herbert Lanese, former president of McDonnell Douglas Corp's McDonnell Douglas Aerospace division, G. Allen Mebane, 67, chairman of Unifi Inc. since 1985 and Jack Nusbaum, chairman of the New York law firm Willkie Farr & Gallagher.

After an hour-long meeting Tuesday between Soros aides, including Druckenmiller, and WMX board members and lawyers at the company's headquarters, the group said the board members "indicated their willingness" to accept two new independent board members to replace resigning members, but failed to agree on who they would be or whether Rooney would be retained.
The group said it may continue to press its case through more talks, coordinated action with other shareholders or solicitation of proxies.
It said it has had talks with Focus Investment Management, L.L.C., a Maine limited liability company that does some of its business under the trade name "Lens" and holds 0.05 percent of WMX stock.

With the group's agreement, it said Lens officials proposed to WMX on February 5 that Lanese and Soros associate Brian Corvese be elected to its board before the company's annual stockholders' meeting in May.
Buntrock had intially told Druckenmiller that Corvese would be acceptable as a director, but that he needed more information about Lanese, which was provided, the group said.

But later Buntrock said he would commit only to hiring an executive search firm to identify two new independent board candidates to seek election at the May meeting, the group said. At that meeting on Feb. 6, Buntrock also changed his postion to say that Lanese was suitable, but Corvese was not, it said.

The group said it has "become even more frustrated with management's lack of progress in enhancing value for (the company's) shareholders and the apparent inability of management, and its recently announced restructuring plan, to address the issue."
